issues.description: Global identifier mismatch: the DD compute-table global variable. The template dd_simulation.py imports a global named `CT` from .dd (line 51 of dd_simulation.py in the template). However, the template's dd.py defines the compute-table global as `_CT` (lines 277-280 in template dd.py) rather than `CT`. The solution repository defines the global as `CT` (lines 279-280 in solution dd.py). This naming mismatch causes an ImportError (or NameError) when running the template code and prevents students from executing or testing the provided starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the compute-table global name consistent across artifacts. Recommended: rename `_CT = ComputeTable()` in the template dd.py to `CT = ComputeTable()` so it matches the import in dd_simulation.py and the solution. Alternatively, modify the import in dd_simulation.py to import `_CT` (e.g. `from .dd import _CT as CT`) — but aligning the template dd.py to define `CT` is the clearer fix for students.

issues.description: The global compute-table object (the same conceptual entity) is named inconsistently across artifacts: in the template repository dd.py the global is declared as `_CT` but dd_simulation.py (template) imports `CT` (from .dd import CT, ...), and the solution repository dd.py declares the global as `CT`. This mismatch ( `_CT` vs `CT` ) prevents the import in dd_simulation.py from resolving the compute-table and will cause an ImportError or confusion for students trying to follow the solution. Students cannot reliably map the compute-table concept in the problem/solution to the template because of the differing identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the global compute-table identifier across files. Rename `_CT = ComputeTable()` in the template dd.py to `CT = ComputeTable()` so dd_simulation.py can import `CT` as written. Alternatively, change the import in dd_simulation.py to import `_CT` and update all usages, but the recommended fix is to rename `_CT` -> `CT` in template/dd.py to match the solution and avoid confusion.
